title: Platform-wide slowness and 429s
executive_summary: Latency and 429s began at ~19:55-20:00Z, coinciding with a ~2.2-2.5x surge in request rate at api-gateway, auth-service and user-service. Logs attribute the surge to client_id=mobile-ios-7.4.0, which the gateway reports as the top client by RPS (up to ~9,500 rps) and whose traffic is flagged as retries with Retry-After ignored. The best-supported explanation is a mobile client retry storm. The user-service release 7.1.3 (19:48Z) is not supported as the cause: user-service latency and error rate were flat through the window, and the change was cosmetic.

hypotheses.description: Retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients that ignore Retry-After, overloading the gateway and downstream auth/user services and triggering rate-limit 429s. Mechanism: Starting ~19:55Z the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client's request volume rises sharply (request_rate 2.2x at gateway, 2.2x at auth, 2.2x at user-service). The gateway flags retries as a large share of that client's traffic with Retry-After ignored, so the retries are not backing off. CPU on the gateway (to ~90%) and auth-service (to ~77-86%) climbs in step, and the gateway begins returning 429s and error rate rises from ~0.5% to ~7%. Causality is consistent with the onset order: client surge at 19:55, then gateway/auth CPU at 19:55-20:00, then 429s at 19:56 and error rate at 19:56.

probable_root_cause.description: Retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients that ignore Retry-After, overloading the gateway and downstream auth/user services and triggering rate-limit 429s.
probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): traffic_surge in api-gateway - Retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients that ignore Retry-After, overloading the gateway and downstream auth/user services and triggering rate-limit 429s.
corrective_actions: Throttle or block mobile-ios-7.4.0 at the gateway (per-client rate limit or client-version block) to stop the retry amplification.
Enforce server-side backoff: return and honour Retry-After, and apply a circuit breaker or 429 shedding at the gateway.
Roll back or hotfix the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client retry behaviour, and coordinate with mobile release owners.
Hold a rollback of user-service 7.1.3 in reserve; roll it back only if the surge is ruled out and user-service degrades.
preventive_actions: Require client SDK tests that verify Retry-After compliance before release.
Add gateway-side retry-budget enforcement per client, with alerts on retry ratio.
Add canary and per-client-version monitoring for mobile releases.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on per-client request rate and retry ratio at api-gateway (threshold, e.g., retries >50% of a client's traffic).
Alert on gateway 429 rate and error rate above 1%.
Monitor gateway and auth CPU, and track p95/p99 latency per endpoint so slowness is not hidden by flat aggregate p99.
Monitor postgres report_rollup() duration as a separate background-load signal.
limitations: No telemetry was queried for postgres, the notification or order services, or the mobile client itself.
Telemetry is aggregated per service; per-client latency was not available.
The 429 log patterns are sampled, so exact 429 volume is unknown.
[agent-reported gap] Release/trigger for mobile-ios-7.4.0 is unknown.
[agent-reported gap] Flat user-service and gateway p99 latency conflicts with the reported slowness and was not explained.
[agent-reported gap] No postgres or DB-side metrics were examined for the report_rollup() statements.
[agent-reported gap] No per-client latency or 429 breakdown was available.
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: INC-011's most likely root cause is a retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients that ignore Retry-After, starting ~19:55Z. This drove a ~2.2x request surge that saturated gateway and auth CPU and produced the 429s and gateway error rate. The user-service 7.1.3 release at 19:48Z is not supported as the cause: its latency, error and timeout metrics are flat, and the traffic surge it coincides with is external. The status is PROBABLE rather than confirmed because the mobile client's release trigger and the cause of the flat p99 latency are not established.
